result:
It struck me today, in the particular blue of the sky at 6:47 in the evening, that I have never once thought about the number 6:47 as a destination. We plan for the 7 o'clock news, for the 8 dinner reservation, for the 10 bedtime story, but the in-between hours — the ones with no label, no appointment, no name — those are where the actual life happens, unrecorded.

I was watching a neighbor's cat walk along a fence line, each step a small negotiation with balance. The cat was not performing. The cat was not being observed by an audience. It was simply a body in the world, doing the thing bodies do, and the world was simply the world. No one had written it down. No one had scored it. It was enough.

And I think that's the thing about the in-between hours. They are the hours where you are allowed to be simply a body in the world. Where the self can loosen its grip, step back, and just be the thing that is warm and looking at a cat on a fence line while the sky does its slow, indifferent turning.

You don't need to justify the hours. You don't need to optimize them. You don't need to extract meaning, though meaning will find you anyway, if you let it, like a cat finding its way back inside through the screen door.

The sky got darker. The cat disappeared. I made tea.

That was the whole evening. That was the whole life, repeated in small, unremarkable pieces.
